Under SGD, E007 measured a ~0.95 pp/epoch slope (H1.5.1 supported), and the 0.08 pp per 1% of time exchange rate was used consistently afterwards. Scoped to SGD: under Muon the slope is 0.54 pp/epoch (E020).
This SGD 9-epoch point no longer bears on the Muon tip.

Its premise (step count is free and more updates help) came from SGD (E010). Under Muon the step count matters much less for accuracy (E022: bs 2000 cost only -0.25 pp), and steps are not free in time because Muon has a per-step cost. The node no longer applies to the tip.
SGD-only prediction with a retired parent. A bs-768 SGD run cannot improve the Muon tip.

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. The strongest schedule lever is lower-resolution early epochs (E006, E021, E026). Measured epoch cost is stepwise in resolution: 16 px 0.32x, 24 px 0.57x, 26 px 0.75x, 28 px 0.79x, 30 px 0.95x of a 32 px epoch (E013, E026). Narrowing high-FLOP layers is refuted (E017), and so is widening late layers (E005). Under Muon, the optimizer adds a fixed per-step cost (~1 ms/step after compiling, E024) that does not shrink with resolution, so it is a larger share of low-res epochs. Reinvesting low-res savings into more 32 px training is untested under Muon: every Muon schedule so far kept 8 total epochs.
updates.reason: Dropped the narrowing lever (refuted by E017), added the 16 px cost point and the Muon per-step cost, and flagged reinvestment as untested in the Muon era, as the review asked.

updates.statement: Progressive resizing makes early epochs much cheaper at little final-accuracy cost, provided the cheap phase uses efficient resolutions (24 px, or 16 px for the first ~2 epochs) rather than 26-28 px. The low-res operator (E016) and final-map geometry (E014) are second-order. Operator: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample, AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1); every shape is compiled and warmed up in build.
updates.reason: E021 (Muon, 4@24+4@32) matched E020 (7@32) in accuracy (-0.04 pp, within noise) at -5% time. The time gain is far outside noise, and SGD showed the same direction (E006, best exchange rate under SGD). Two optimizers agree, so it is supported. The 'reinvest in more epochs' clause is moved to a separate untested node.
This SGD 24->28->32 prediction is superseded. E013/E014 showed 26-28 px phases are inefficient, and the two-stage Muon schedules (E021, E026) replaced it.
Superseded. E021 (Muon, 4@24+4@32 at 8.0 epochs) already reached 0.7578 at 6.33 s. The 9.5-10 epoch SGD version would not beat the current 5.5 s tip.

updates.statement: In the tip code (E026 lineage), the flip/translate/resize augmentation RNG comes from the trial seed and is reset in prepare. A logged hash of the first batch's augmentation parameters differs across seeds 0-2, and repeating seed 0 reproduces it. E006's 0.02 pp per-seed spread was chance.
updates.reason: Rescoped to the tip, since the tip's lineage descends from E006's operator. Later runs with the same operator show normal per-seed spreads (E014 0.76 pp, E021 0.9 pp, E025 0.85 pp), so shared streams are unlikely. The hash was never reported, though, so this stays open as a cheap compliance check.

updates.statement: At full resolution this A100-SXM4 trains at its 400 W power cap (SM ~1335-1380 MHz), so time for the network's own fwd/bwd tracks GPU energy (FLOPs + bytes). CPU gaps hidden behind GPU work cost nothing (E004, E010, E011). This model is incomplete: launch-bound phases that leave the GPU idle for whole milliseconds do cost time (eager Muon, ~2 ms/step, E019; compiling and batching it cut 5.3%, E024, confounded with a 3.8->1.67 ms GPU-time cut). Small-map 16/24 px phases may be launch- or per-step-bound rather than power-bound (unmeasured). Risk that cannot be tested here: the official 300 W PCIe card may shift the relative costs of resolutions and of Muon overhead.
updates.reason: E019 and E024 contradict the blanket 'energy-only' model in the Muon regime. Restated to cover both regimes and to note the hardware-transfer risk from the review.

updates.statement: NVML sampling at >=10 Hz during an untimed run of the E026 tip shows board power >=95% of the 400 W cap for >=80% of the 32 px phase. During the 16 px and 24 px phases power stays below 90% of the cap for >=30% of the time, i.e. those phases are launch- or per-step-bound. Observational only; no sleeps or idle gaps added.
updates.reason: Retargeted at the current tip. Now that the schedule includes 16 px, this measurement decides whether per-step overhead cuts (Muon, whole-step compile) pay off in the low-res phases.
E017: narrowing group 2 cost 0.94 pp for 8.2% of time (0.115 pp per 1%), worse than every alternative lever. The 0.94 pp loss is about 4x the perturbation noise on a deterministic SGD base.
E017: -0.94 pp against the <=0.4 pp bar, far beyond noise.

E025 (5@24+3@32 vs 4@24+4@32) lost 0.51 pp; using the averaged E021/E024 baseline the loss is ~0.42 pp. Both exceed the pre-registered 0.3 pp. Under Muon the share of training at 32 px is close to binding. A restated mechanism (binding 32 px tail, nearly free first epochs) replaces it as a new node.
Its parent is refuted and the prediction was framed for E006/SGD. The reinvestment question under Muon is now a new Lvl3.

updates.statement: Resolutions below 24 px are disproportionately cheap (16 px = 0.32x of a 32 px epoch, E026), and the first ~2 epochs tolerate 16 px well. A third 16 px epoch costs more (E029: -0.31 pp for -4.8%, 0.065 pp per 1% of time). With E028's rerun averaged in, the first two 16 px swaps cost ~0.40-0.51 pp for -8.3% (0.05-0.06 pp per 1%), not clearly better than the 24<-32 swap (E025: 0.078). The difference is within ~+/-0.03 pp per 1%. E026 dominates E025 on time only.
updates.reason: E026 supports the cost claim and the claim that early 16 px phases are cheap in accuracy. The review is right that the '2x better exchange rate' claim does not survive the E028 rerun, so confidence is held moderate.

The 16 px epoch cost 0.32x (bar <=0.35x). 2@16+2@24+4@32 reached >=0.753 at <=6.3 s twice: E026 0.7565 / 5.50 s and E028 rerun 0.7543 / 5.52 s. Both runs clear the bar, so this is not a single result within noise. The 20 px cost was never measured; that part is unresolved. E029 (3@16) is inconclusive and does not bear on this schedule.
E023: tanh-approximate GELU was 5.1% slower than exact erf under Inductor, with equal accuracy. Exact erf is the cheaper GELU on this stack.
E023: time +5.1% against a predicted >=1% saving. The difference is far outside time noise.

updates.statement: (SGD full-res regime) Fixed and per-step CPU/launch overhead (timed prepare, Python/kernel-launch overhead, separate optimizer kernels) is a measurable share of the ~7 s SGD run, and removing it cuts time without touching accuracy.
updates.reason: Still refuted for the SGD full-res regime (E004, E010, E011; the Fable write-up also found CUDA graphs and fusion worth ~0). The Muon overhead (E019, E024) and possible launch-bound low-res phases are tracked under the new optimizer Lvl1 and under H2.4/H2.4.1, so the scope here is narrowed instead of reopened.

updates.statement: Zero-time-cost accuracy levers can buy 0.2-0.5 pp of slack to spend on resolution or epoch cuts. Under SGD at 8 full-res epochs they gave nothing (E008, E009, E015). Under Muon + progressive resizing they are untested, and the regime is different: Muon fits faster, and tuned public Muon recipes use LS 0.09 (vs our 0.3), an LR floor of 0.05 and a short final EMA. Muon's own hyperparameters belong to the optimizer Lvl1.
updates.reason: The null results were all under SGD, and the review notes that retuning is live again under Muon. BN re-estimation (H6.2) is refuted. LS, LR floor and EMA horizon remain untested on the tip.

E018: BN re-estimation lost 0.34 pp on a deterministic SGD base, and the mechanism is understood. With bn_momentum 0.6 the running stats reflect only the last ~5 steps at 32 px, so low-res epochs leave no stale statistics to fix.
E018: -0.34 pp against the predicted >=+0.2 pp, in the opposite direction.

new.statement: Optimizer quality per update is the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~8 epochs (the short schedule under-fits, E008). Muon on the 9 group 3x3 convs is the main lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter accuracy-vs-epochs slope (0.54 vs 0.95 pp/epoch, E020), and tolerance of large batches (E022: -0.25 pp at bs 2000 vs SGD's -0.81). Its hyperparameters are sensitive (E027: momentum 0.85 cost 1.18 pp) and were tuned for CIFAR-10 at bs 2000 without lookahead, so both accuracy per epoch and Muon's remaining per-step cost (~1 ms/step, ~7% of time) still have room.

Muon momentum is already near its optimum at 0.6-0.65. Both independently tuned public Muon recipes chose 0.655 (hiverge, Fable E1), and E027 showed the high side is steep. LR is the less explored knob: the public recipes use 0.205-0.2255, below our 0.24.

On the E026 tip, Muon momentum 0.5 (lr 0.24, Nesterov, everything else unchanged) gives a 3-seed accuracy no higher than 0.7574 (tip estimate 0.7554 + 0.2 pp) at equal time. Lowering momentum does not buy usable slack.
On the E026 tip, Muon lr 0.20 (momentum 0.6) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7575 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7554 estimate) at equal time (+/-1%).

The Muon overhead left after E024 (~1 ms/step x 384 steps, ~0.4 s, ~7%) can be cut at near-equal math. Options: renormalize weights every 2->17 steps instead of every step (hiverge, Fable), use 2 Newton-Schulz steps with better coefficients (Polar Express, Turbo-Muon AOL), or use a larger batch. The cost is fixed per step, so it is a larger share of the 16/24 px epochs.

On the E026 tip, renormalizing Muon weights every 2 + int(15*progress) steps instead of every step (inside the compiled update, with the step flag passed as a tensor so nothing recompiles) cuts time by >=1.5% with a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535.

On the E026 tip, 2 Newton-Schulz steps with per-iteration Polar-Express-style coefficients (instead of 3 fixed-coefficient steps) cut time by >=2% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.2 pp against the 0.7554 estimate.

On the compiled-Muon E026 tip, bs 1536 (SGD groups scaled by the kilostep rule, Muon lr/momentum unchanged, LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count) cuts time by >=3% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.25 pp against the 0.7554 estimate.

Under Muon the 32 px tail is binding: removing one 32 px epoch costs ~0.4-0.5 pp (E025), while the first ~2 epochs tolerate 16 px (E026) and the third less so (E029). Low-res savings are therefore best reinvested in a longer 32 px tail with switch points at fractional, step-indexed positions, so the schedule can land just above the threshold instead of moving in whole-epoch (0.3-0.85 s) chunks.

A 4@16 + 4.5@32 px schedule (8.5 total epochs, step-indexed switch, LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count, E026 operator and compiled Muon) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.755 at time <=5.45 s (estimate: 4x0.27 + 4.5x0.85 + Muon/fixed overhead).

An untimed compiled cost measurement (2 epochs each) shows a 12 px epoch >=0.22x and a 20 px epoch 0.40-0.50x the cost of a 32 px epoch. The floor comes from Muon's fixed per-step cost and from small-kernel inefficiency, so replacing a 16 px epoch with 12 px saves <1.5% of total time and is not worth pursuing.

The tip's run-to-run non-determinism (E028) comes from per-process autotuning: max-autotune configs for the compiled Muon update (bmm, Triton reductions), or cuDNN/Inductor algorithm picks for the newer 16/24 px shapes. The SGD 32 px recipe compiled the same way was bit-identical (E002). Pinning these choices in build restores determinism, which makes seed-paired comparisons possible again and roughly halves the noise on a difference between two runs.

With the Muon update compiled without max-autotune (mode='default') and cuDNN algorithm selection pinned (cudnn.benchmark=False or deterministic algorithms for the 16/24/32 px shapes), two identical runs of the tip give bit-identical per-seed accuracies, with time within +1.5% of 5.50 s.
LS 0.3 was found optimal under SGD (E009, futurebiohackers sweep). Muon fits faster and tuned public Muon recipes use LS 0.09, so the tip may be over-regularized.
On the E026 tip, label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3 gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7575 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7554 estimate) at equal time.

structured_output.summary:
I revised the tree to match the Muon era.

**Muon.** H5, H5.1 and H5.1.1 are now refuted. E019, E020 and E024 show that Muon greatly improves time to 75%, and their evidence tokens were logged with the wrong sign. The finding moves to a new Lvl1, N1: optimizer quality per update is the binding constraint. N1 has two mechanisms:
- **Hyperparameters (N1a):** momentum is probably near its optimum, since both tuned public recipes use 0.655. LR has not been explored.
- **Remaining overhead (N1b):** about 1 ms/step, roughly 7% of time. The candidate cuts are periodic weight renormalization, 2 Newton-Schulz steps with better coefficients, and bs 1536.

**Noise model.** H4 is rewritten. The tip is not deterministic between runs (E028). The sd of a 3-seed mean is about 0.15 pp and the sd of a difference between two runs is about 0.2 pp. The tip estimate is 0.7554 on seeds 0-2 (0.7553 over 11 seeds). H4 now carries the rule for a new tip: a 3-seed mean of at least 0.755, or two runs averaging at least 0.7535. H4.1 is supported only for SGD. A new node, N3, proposes that pinning the autotune choices would restore bit-determinism.

**SGD-era nodes.** H1 is scoped to SGD, where it is supported. Retiring its SGD-only children removes H1.5.2, H1.6 and H1.6.1. H3 is scoped to SGD at full resolution and stays refuted. H2.4 now admits that launch-bound Muon phases do cost time. H2.4.1 is retargeted at the tip's 16/24 px phases.

**Status cleanup.**
- H2.6 and H2.6.1 are refuted (E017).
- H6.2 and H6.2.1 are refuted (E018).
- H2.9 and H2.9.1 are refuted (E023).
- H2.7 is refuted (E025), and a new node N2 replaces it: the 32 px tail is binding, so savings should be reinvested with step-indexed switching.
- H2.1 is supported (E021, consistent with E006).
- H2.8.1 is supported on two feasible runs (E026, E028). Its 20 px cost is still unmeasured.
- H2.8 is reworded so that its 16 px exchange-rate advantage is not overstated.
- H2.1.3 stays open as a cheap compliance check.
- H2.1.1, H2.1.4, H2.7.1, H4.2.1 and H4.2.2 are retired as superseded.

**Regularization.** H6 is reopened for the Muon regime. Its new child N4 tests whether LS 0.2 helps the tip.

The open Lvl1 hypotheses are H2, H4, H6 and N1.
